origin_derivations.WT-1: Session.init/1 is the only backend assignment (options.backend, default HTTP.WebTransport.Transport.QUIC). New sites migrate (202), handle_message (203) and acknowledge (204) call that retained module after function_exported?/3 checks. backend_or_invalid_state/2 (205) and finish_send/3 (206) invoke only the local closures built in handle_call/3 around the same retained backend; close moved to cleanup_backend/2 (ID 159) and the send-close/abort closures moved to finish_send/3 (IDs 163/164). The sole library backend now opens a real exclusive HTTP3 ConnectionOwner with a Quic.Cleanup.new/1 descriptor, literal webtransport session options and caller ssl keywords validated by SSL.QUIC.Config; its stream/datagram/migration bodies are literal ConnectionOwner and Cleanup calls covered by H3-1/H3-2/Q1. rc.13 follow-up (89107e7): occurrence 166 (state.backend.get_stats/1) is removed because :get_stats now replies from session-kept counters; the other thirteen retained-backend sites keep their expressions and twelve move by 4 to 41 lines. Transport.QUIC runs owner calls through interruptible/1, which spawns a monitored helper around a literal closure; its fun.() calls only the closures built at the three literal call sites and is not a reviewed occurrence.
origin_derivations.HTTP-1_HTTP-4: Alt-Svc keeps tls_backend nil only until the TCP fallback pins it through TLSBackend.resolve/1, which accepts only ExSSL. HTTP/3 options lift ex_ssl reference identity into QUIC ssl data. SocketClient transport/protocol selectors and the H3 handler are unchanged; 12 SocketClient sites move. rc.13 follow-ups (e95bb5c, cff6e9a): HTTP/1 redirect parity and the HTTP/2 retry add only literal bookkeeping; the same twelve SocketClient sites move by 66 or 68 lines with unchanged expressions and selectors. rc.14 follow-up (c7fada8): HTTP.TLSBackend and the tls_backend option are removed; Dialer.select_transport/2 names the literal HTTP.Transport.ExSSL, so the TLS selector is a literal module rather than a single-valued resolver. The twelve SocketClient sites move by 5, 6 or 10 lines with unchanged expressions and selectors. rc.14 follow-up (5eae73d): the retry loop adds only the literal attempt-owner bookkeeping; the twelve SocketClient sites move by 10 lines with unchanged expressions and selectors. rc.16 follow-up (a14c711): the http2_unprocessed_retry option adds only a literal Keyword.get/3 guard and a literal HTTP.Telemetry.http2_unprocessed_retry/3 call; the twelve SocketClient sites move by 5 lines with unchanged expressions and selectors.
origin_derivations.HTTP-9: WebSocket over HTTP/3 leaves tls_backend unresolved; Runtime.Options rejects any explicit backend for HTTP/3 and the HTTP1 selector still maps only :ex_ssl. Seven WebSocket sites move with unchanged expressions. rc.13 follow-up (c08c93f): the seven WebSocket.Connection sites move by 7 or 12 lines with unchanged expressions. The nine HTTP-3 EventSource.Connection sites (e03c828) likewise keep their retained transport selectors and move by 1 to 34 lines. rc.14 follow-up (c7fada8, c222551): WebSocket and EventSource select_transport/1 name the literal HTTP.Transport.ExSSL; five WebSocket.Connection sites move by 3 lines and the nine EventSource.Connection sites by 2 or 5 lines, all with unchanged expressions.
origin_derivations.HTTP-2: The nine RequestLifecycle worker producers are unchanged in number and kind.
origin_derivations.HTTP-5: then/3 accepts only a 1-arity success function and nil or a 1-arity error function (is_function/2 guards) and appends them to the callbacks list of the returned promise. HTTP.fetch/2 builds the only production %HTTP.Promise{} with callbacks: []; then/3 is the only writer. await/2 runs the retained callbacks in the awaiting caller process: run_callbacks/3 invokes error_fun.(reason) (207) only when is_function(error_fun, 1) and success_fun.(value) (106, previously the apply/2 in apply_callback/2) otherwise. Results are interpreted only as a Promise to settle or ordinary data; a returned function is never invoked. The callbacks are caller-supplied public-API callbacks, the same approved boundary as before. rc.14 follow-up (8f35305): await/2 reports its own wait expiry as :await_timeout; both invocations move by 3 lines with unchanged expressions.
origin_derivations.HTTP-11: HTTP.Retry.normalize/3 is the only constructor of %HTTP.Retry{} (struct literal at its sole return). normalize_mode/1 stores a function only when is_function(fun, 2) holds for the caller `retry:` value; every other value is :transient, :safe_transient, nil or an ArgumentError. normalize_delay/1 stores a function only when is_function(fun, 1) holds for the caller `retry_delay:` value; otherwise nil, a non-negative integer or an ArgumentError. FetchOptions.normalize_options/1 validates both through normalize/3 and retry_policy/1 rebuilds the policy through normalize/3 again; HTTP.fetch/2 passes that policy to the task closure, handle_async_request/6 stores it unchanged in the attempts map and run_attempts/3 passes it to HTTP.Retry.decide/5, which only reads it. retry?/3 (209) invokes fun.(request, result) only in the is_function(fun, 2) clause, after the built-in hard rules (max_retries, no streamed or half-duplex body, no :aborted or :timeout) and never for a built-in mode; configured_delay/2 (210) invokes fun.(attempt) only after the nil and integer clauses, so its argument is the normalized 1-arity function. Both results are data: a non-boolean or a non-integer/negative delay raises ArgumentError in the Promise worker, and the delay is still bounded by the request deadline. No library caller supplies either function; they are caller-supplied public-API callbacks, the same approved boundary as the HTTP-5 Promise callbacks. HTTP.Retry is @moduledoc false and HTTP.handle_async_request/6 is @doc false; the only production callers are HTTP.fetch/2 and run_attempts/3, and a manually constructed policy is not supported input.
